questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam is a cool place to live and study. It was both important for me to live in a nice city with a lot of opportunities to go out and meet new people and also to study at a university where the courses sounded interesting and relevant.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. I do not recall any trouble in this regard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails and there was a student desk where you could ask questions at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got help from the host university. It seems very difficult and expensive to find housing in Amsterdam on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: No one lives on campus. The place where I lived was primarily exchange students and a lot of social activities were offered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The shared kitchen was not a great experience. It seems that it is very normal in Amsterdam to have mice in your homes. We had mice in the shared kitchen. This was really gross.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was really easy and intuitive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration was online. You could pick more courses than you needed and then afterwards, it was possible to de-register from courses if you had too many or if some overlapped. There was also a second round of registration if you did not get the courses you needed/hoped to get.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not need help and therefore, do not know this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I had to have five courses of 6 ECTS points each and got five courses that I was happy with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for all courses you want and check if they overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some very interesting courses and the teachers/professors were skilled.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were in general of a high academic level. I had three courses in the first block and two courses in the second block. The first block was challenging since three courses are a lot of reading. I heard from other students that most people only have two in a block but as an exchange student you need to have five all together to get 30 ECTS points in total.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was either just a weekly lecture or a combination of a lecture and a workgroup. The workgroup is familiar to the seminar classes at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. EU Company Law (block 1)
2. EU Migration Law, forced and unforced migration (block 1)
3. EU Regulated Markets (block 1)
4. Advanced EU Competition Law (block 2)
5. Finance, Insolvency, and Security (block 2)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: This of course depends on what your interests are. I liked EU Company Law and Finance, Insolvency, and Security the best. These two courses were the only ones of the five I took that had both a weekly lecture and a workgroup. I think the workgroups were very good since that allowed for interaction and I learned a lot from this. The teachers in both of these courses were also the best I had in my entire stay. Very skilled in their areas of the law and very good at teaching difficult materials. Company Law was a bit more theoretical and less practical than what I have experienced before, this provided good perspective on company laws in general. Finance was probably the most difficult course I had, but at the same time my favourite.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spent almost nothing on books since most of the materials are made available online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of social activities through Erasmus. There was also the possibility to join a student gym which I think would be cheaper than regular gyms.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The night life in Amsterdam is very good. There are a lot of techno festivals, clubs etc. if you like that. The restaurants and cafés were also very good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: This depends on where you come from. A lot of students from America, Australia or other places far away did a lot of trips around Europe to see more European cities when to take advantage of the close distance. I did not do trips to other countries, but I would recommend trips to other Dutch cities. It is cheap and easy to get around the Netherlands by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialize a lot with the Dutch students, but my experience is that most people are very helpful and wants to talk to you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the bike culture. I appreciated that I was not dependent on public transportation. I also felt very safe in the city to go out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, keep up in your courses. There is no real exam prep period so if you are far behind, this will be very difficult to catch up on. Second, get a bike as soon as you arrive. Third, go out and enjoy the city. There are a lot of fun places!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It rains a lot in Amsterdam. The first months were really terrible weather, but summer is amazing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have gotten some very good friends from my exchange. I also learned a lot from the courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bad weather in the first half of the exchange and the mice in our homes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
